Order was created and established simultaneously with the substances. And those in whom pure act was produced were the summit of the world.
Pure potential held the lowest place. In the middle, potential was bound together with act by such a bond that it will never be undone.
Jerome wrote for you that the angels were created long ages before the rest of the world was made.
But this truth I speak is written on many pages by the scribes of the Holy Spirit — and you will find it if you look carefully.
And reason also can see it to some degree, for it would not allow that the movers of the heavens should exist so long without their perfection.
Now you know where and when these loves were created, and how — so that three flames of your desire are already quenched.
One could not count to twenty before a part of the angels brought turmoil to the foundation of your elements.
The rest remained and began the art you see here, with such delight that they never cease their circling.
The origin of the Fall was the accursed pride of the one you saw crushed by the weight of all the world.
Those you see here were humble enough to acknowledge themselves as coming from the Goodness that had made them capable of such vast understanding.
And so their vision was exalted by illuminating grace and by their own merit, so that they have full and steadfast will.
And I do not want you to doubt, but to be certain, that receiving grace is meritorious in proportion to how much affection opens itself to it.
Now you can contemplate much of this assembly, if my words have been taken in, without further help.
But since in your schools on earth it is taught that the angelic nature has understanding, memory, and will,
I will speak further so that you may see the pure truth which down there is confused by the ambiguity of that teaching.
These beings, from the moment they first rejoiced in the face of God, have never turned their sight from it — from which nothing is hidden.
And therefore their vision is never interrupted by any new object. And therefore they have no need to remember by recalling divided thought.
So down there people dream while awake — some believing they speak truth and some not, and in the latter lies the greater fault and shame.
You mortals do not walk along one path when you philosophize — so much does the love of display and the thought of it carry you away.
And even this is tolerated here with less anger than when the divine Scripture is set aside or twisted.
No one thinks down there about how much blood it costs to sow it in the world, or how pleasing is the one who humbly keeps close to it.
Everyone strains for show and invents his own ideas, and these are expounded and expanded by the preachers — while the Gospel is silent.
One says that the moon moved backward at the Passion of Christ and interposed itself to block the light.
And he lies, for the light hid itself on its own. And so to the Spaniards and the Indians, as well as to the Jews, this eclipse appeared.
Florence does not have as many Lapos and Bindos as the fables like these that every year are cried from the pulpits on all sides.
So the poor sheep, who know nothing, come home from their pasture fed on wind — and not seeing the harm does not excuse them.
Christ did not say to His first company: 'Go and preach idle stories to the world.' He gave them the true foundation.
And that alone rang from their lips, so that in the fight to kindle faith they made the Gospel both their shield and lance.
Now men go forth to preach with jests and clowning, and as long as there is a good laugh, the cowl puffs up and nothing more is asked.
But such a bird is nesting in the tail of that hood that if the congregation could see it, they would know what kind of pardons they are trusting in.
Because of this, such folly has grown on earth that without any proof of trustworthiness, they would flock to any promise.
On this Saint Anthony fattens his pig, and others too, who are far more piggish — paying with money that bears no stamp of value.
But since we have digressed enough, turn your eyes back now to the straight road, so that the journey may be shortened with the time.
The angelic nature steps forward in such a vast number that mortal speech and mortal thought can never reach so far.
And if you consider what Daniel reveals, you will see that in his thousands any precise number is obscured.
The Primal Light that irradiates them all is received by them in as many ways as there are splendors to which it joins itself.
And since affection follows the act of understanding, the sweetness of love blazes differently in each, some more and some less.
See now the height and the breadth of the Eternal Goodness — which has made itself so many mirrors in which it is reflected,
While remaining in itself One, as it was before.

chapters.title: Paradiso, Canto XXX
paragraphs: Perhaps six thousand miles away from us, the sixth hour is ablaze, and this world already tilts its shadow nearly level,
When the center of the deep sky, high above us, begins to change so that here and there a star can no longer be seen at this floor of earth.
And as the brightest handmaid of the sun advances further, so the sky shuts off its lights one by one, down to the most beautiful.
Not otherwise the triumph that plays forever around the Point that overcame me — seeming enclosed by that which it encloses —
Little by little faded from my sight. And so my seeing nothing, and my love, compelled me to turn my eyes back to Beatrice.
If everything that has been said of her up to this point were compressed into a single act of praise, it would be too slight to serve this turn.
The beauty I saw transcends all measure — not only beyond ours, but I truly believe that only its Maker enjoys it in its entirety.
At this pass I confess myself defeated, more than any poet — whether comic or tragic — was ever defeated by a point in his theme.
For as the sun does to the most trembling eye, so the memory of that sweet smile strips my mind of its very self.
From the first day I saw her face in this life to this present sight, the pursuit of my song has never been cut short.
But now my pursuit must desist from following her beauty further in my verse, as every artist must at the limit of his skill.
Such as I leave her for a mightier trumpet than mine — which is bringing its arduous subject to a close —
With the voice and manner of a leader whose task is done, she began again: "We have emerged from the greatest body into the heaven that is pure light.
Light of the intellect, full of love. Love of the true good, full of joy. Joy that transcends every sweetness.
Here you will see both hosts of Paradise, and one of them in the form you will see it at the Final Judgment."
As a sudden flash of lightning scatters the spirits of sight and strips the eye of the power to perceive even the strongest objects,
So a living light blazed around me, wrapping me in such a veil of its own radiance that nothing was visible to me.
"The love that quiets this heaven always welcomes souls into itself with such a greeting, to prepare the candle for its flame."
No sooner had these brief words reached me than I felt myself rising beyond my own power.
And I was kindled with such new vision that there is no light so bright that my eyes could not have withstood it.
And I saw a light in the form of a river, blazing with splendor, between two banks painted with marvelous spring.
From this river living sparks were darting, and on every side they settled into the flowers, like rubies set in gold.
Then, as if drunk with the fragrances, they plunged back again into the wondrous flood, and as one entered, another flew out.
"The high desire that now inflames and presses you to understand what you are seeing pleases me all the more the more it swells.
But you must drink of this water before such great thirst in you can be quenched." So spoke the sun of my eyes.
Then she added: "The river and the topazes that enter and leave it, and the laughter of the grasses are shadowy prefaces of their truth.
Not that these things are difficult in themselves. The deficiency is in you — your sight is not yet risen high enough."
No baby who has slept too long ever turned its face so eagerly toward its milk as I did then, bending down to the water that flows there for our betterment.
And the moment my eyelids drank of it, it seemed to me that its length was transformed into roundness.
Then, as people who have been wearing masks seem changed when they remove the disguise that hid their true appearance,
So the flowers and the sparks changed before me into a greater festival, and I saw both courts of heaven made plain.
O splendor of God, through which I saw the high triumph of the true kingdom — give me the power to tell what I saw!
There is a light up there that makes the Creator visible to every creature whose peace lies only in seeing Him.
And it spreads into so vast a circle that its circumference would be too loose a belt around the sun.
Its whole appearance is made up of a ray reflected from the summit of the Primum Mobile, which draws from it its life and power.
And as a hillside mirrors itself in water at its base, as if to see its own adornment when it is richest in grass and flowers,
So, mirrored in that light, rising above it in more than a thousand tiers, I saw all that has returned of us up there.
And if the lowest row gathers within itself so great a light, how vast is the spread of this rose in its outermost petals!
My sight did not lose itself in the breadth and height, but took in the full scope and quality of that rejoicing.
There, near and far neither add nor subtract. For where God directly governs, natural law has no relevance.
Into the yellow of the eternal Rose, which spreads and rises and breathes a fragrance of praise to the ever-vernal Sun,
Like one who is silent yet longs to speak, Beatrice drew me, and said: "Behold how vast the gathering of white robes!
See how great the circuit of our city! See how full our seats already are, overflowing!
So that few more are now awaited here!
On that great throne on which your eyes are fixed, because of the crown already placed upon it,
Before you take your seat at this wedding feast, shall sit the soul — destined to be Augustus on earth — of the noble Henry, who will come to set Italy right before she is ready.
Blind greed, which casts its spell upon you, has made you like the little child who dies of hunger and drives away the nurse.
And at that time the prefect of the sacred court will be one who, openly or covertly, will not walk the same road with him.
But God will not endure him long in that holy office. He will be thrust down to where Simon Magus pays for his crimes,
And he will push the one from Anagni even deeper."

chapters.title: Paradiso, Canto XXXI
paragraphs: In the form, then, of a white rose, the saintly host displayed itself to me — the host whom Christ made His bride with His own blood.
But the other host — the angels — which as it flies sees and sings the glory of the One who fills it with love, and the goodness that made it so noble,
Like a swarm of bees that one moment sinks into the flowers and the next returns to where its labor is turned into sweetness,
Descended into the great flower adorned with so many petals, and rose again to the place where its love abides forevermore.
Their faces were all of living flame, their wings of gold, and the rest so white that no snow has ever reached that purity.
From tier to tier, descending into the flower, they carried something of the peace and ardor they gathered by fanning their wings.
Nor did this multitude of flying forms, interposing themselves between the flower and what was above, obstruct the sight or the splendor.
For the divine light penetrates the universe according to its worthiness, so that nothing can stand as a barrier against it.
This realm of security and gladness, filled with people ancient and modern, directed all its gaze and all its love toward a single mark.
O Threefold Light, sparkling in a single star upon their sight, which so satisfies them — look down upon our tempest here below!
If the barbarians, coming from that region which Helice covers every day as she revolves overhead with her beloved son,
Were struck with wonder when they beheld Rome and all her noble works — at the time when the Lateran surpassed all mortal things —
Then I, who had come to the divine from the human, from time to eternity, from Florence to a people just and sane,
With what amazement must I have been filled! Truly, between the wonder and the joy, it pleased me neither to hear nor to speak.
And as a pilgrim who finds renewal in gazing round the temple of his vow, and hopes one day to tell how it was,
So, making my way through the living light, I directed my eyes across all the ranks — now upward, now downward, now all around.
I saw faces shaped by charity, embellished by Another's light and by their own smiles, and gestures graced with every dignity.
My gaze had already taken in the general form of Paradise as a whole, without having fixed on any single part.
And I turned with rekindled desire to question my Lady about things that kept my mind in suspense.
One thing I expected, and another answered me. I thought I would see Beatrice, but instead I saw an old man, dressed like the glorious host.
His eyes and cheeks were overflowing with benign joy, and his bearing was tender and fatherly.
"Where is she?" I asked at once. And he replied: "To bring your longing to its end, Beatrice sent me from my place.
And if you look up to the third tier of the highest row, you will see her again, upon the throne her merits have assigned her."
Without a word I raised my eyes and saw her, making herself a crown by reflecting from herself the eternal rays.
From the highest region where the thunder roars, no mortal eye is as far removed, even in the deepest sea,
As my sight was from Beatrice there. But distance made no difference, because her image came down to me undimmed by any medium.
"O Lady, in whom my hope is strong, and who for my salvation endured to leave the imprint of your feet in Hell,
Of all the things I have beheld, I recognize that the grace and virtue came from your power and your goodness.
You brought me from slavery to freedom by every path and every means within your power to use.
Preserve your magnificence toward me, so that this soul of mine, which you have healed, may be pleasing to you when it is released from the body."
So I prayed. And she, so far away, seemed to smile and look at me once more. Then she turned back to the eternal fountain.
And the holy old man said: "So that you may perfectly complete your journey — the one to which prayer and holy love have sent me —
Fly with your eyes all around this garden. For gazing on it will prepare your sight to rise further along the divine ray.
And the Queen of Heaven, for whom I burn wholly with love, will grant us every grace, because I am her faithful Bernard."
As someone who comes perhaps from Croatia to gaze at our Veronica, and whose ancient hunger is never sated,
And who says in thought, while the relic is displayed: 'My Lord Jesus Christ, true God, was this then what your face looked like?'
Such was I, gazing at the living charity of the man who, in this world, through contemplation, tasted that peace.
"Son of grace," he began, "this joyful existence will not be known to you if you keep your eyes fixed only down here at the lowest place.
Rather, look upon the circles all the way to the most remote, until you see the Queen enthroned — she to whom this realm is devoted and subject."
I raised my eyes. And as at dawn the eastern part of the horizon outshines the part where the sun goes down,
So, as if moving with my eyes from valley to mountaintop, I saw one part at the far edge surpass in splendor all the rest.
And just as the sky blazes brightest where we expect the pole of the chariot that Phaethon drove so badly, while the light diminishes on either side,
So that peaceful banner of flame gleamed brightest at the center and tapered equally on both sides.
And at that center, with wings spread wide, I saw more than a thousand jubilant angels, each one different in radiance and in kind.
I saw there, smiling at their songs and their play, a beauty that was the delight within the eyes of all the other saints.
And even if I had as great a wealth in speech as in imagination, I would not dare attempt the smallest part of her loveliness.
Bernard, the moment he saw my eyes fixed and intent upon the object of his own burning devotion, turned his own eyes to her with such love
That it made mine more ardent to behold.

chapters.title: Paradiso, Canto XXXII
paragraphs: Absorbed in his delight, that contemplative soul took up the willing role of teacher and began his holy instruction:
"The wound that Mary closed and anointed was opened and inflicted by the one who sits so beautiful at her feet — that is Eve.
In the order of seats that the third row makes, Rachel is seated, lower than the other, with Beatrice, as you can see.
Sarah, Rebecca, Judith, and the woman who was the ancestress of the Singer who cried 'Miserere mei' in grief for his sin —
You can see them descending from tier to tier, as I go down through the Rose from petal to petal, naming each one.
And from the seventh row downward, just as from above it, Hebrew women follow in succession, dividing all the tresses of the flower.
Because, according to the direction in which their faith looked toward Christ, these women form the dividing wall by which the sacred stairways are separated.
On this side, where the flower is complete in every petal, are seated those who believed in Christ who was still to come.
On the other side, where the semicircles are broken by empty spaces, are those who turned their faces toward Christ already come.
And as on this side the glorious throne of the Lady of Heaven, and the seats below it, create so great a dividing line,
So, opposite, does the seat of the great John — who, ever holy, endured the desert and martyrdom, and then two years in Limbo.
And beneath him, chosen to create this division, sit Francis, Benedict, and Augustine, and others, descending from tier to tier all the way down to us.
Now behold the depth of divine Providence! For both aspects of the faith will fill this garden in equal measure.
And know that downward from the row that cuts through the middle of both halves, the souls are not seated by their own merit.
They are seated by another's, under fixed conditions. For these are spirits absolved before they could exercise any true choice.
You can recognize this in their faces and in their childlike voices, if you look at them closely and listen.
Now you are troubled, and in your troubling you are silent. But I will untie the tight knot in which your subtle thoughts have bound you.
Within the vastness of this realm, no random point can find a place — any more than sadness, or thirst, or hunger can.
For everything you see has been established by eternal law, so that the ring fits the finger precisely.
And therefore these souls, hurried early to true life, are not placed here 'without cause,' ranked as more or less excellent among themselves.
The King, through whom this realm rests in so great a love and so great a delight that no will dares to ask for more,
Creating every mind in His own joyful sight, endows them with grace in different measure, as He pleases. And here let the fact suffice.
And this is noted clearly and explicitly for you in Holy Scripture, in the case of those twins who, still within their mother, had their anger roused.
Therefore, according to the color of the hair — that is, according to the quality of grace — the supreme light consents that they be fittingly crowned.
Without, then, any merit from their deeds, they are stationed in different ranks, differing only in the sharpness of their first perception.
In the earliest centuries, the faith of the parents alone was sufficient, along with innocence, to secure the salvation of their children.
After those first ages were completed, it was necessary for males to add the virtue of circumcision to their innocent wings.
But after the time of grace had come, without the perfect baptism of Christ, such innocence was held back below.
Now look into the face that most resembles Christ. For only its brightness can prepare you to see Christ Himself."
I saw such immense gladness rain down upon her, carried by the holy minds created to fly through those heights,
That nothing I had seen before held me in such wonder or showed me such a likeness of God.
And the same Love that first descended to her, singing 'Ave Maria, gratia plena,' spread its wings wide before her.
From every side the blessed court responded to this divine song, so that every face became more serene.
"O holy father, who endures for my sake to be down here, leaving the sweet place in which you sit by eternal lot,
Who is the angel that with such joy gazes into the eyes of our Queen, so enamored that he seems made of fire?"
So I had recourse again to the teaching of the one who drew his beauty from Mary, as the morning star draws beauty from the sun.
And he said to me: "All the grace and gallantry that can exist in an angel or a soul is entirely in him. And we would have it so.
For he is the one who bore the palm down to Mary, when the Son of God resolved to take our burden upon Himself.
But now follow with your eyes as I speak, and note the great patricians of this most just and merciful empire.
Those two who sit highest up, the most enraptured, being nearest to the Empress, are like two roots of this Rose.
The one placed near her on the left is the father whose reckless tasting caused the human race to taste so much bitterness — Adam.
On the right you see that ancient father of Holy Church to whom Christ entrusted the keys of this lovely flower — Peter.
And the one who saw all the evil days, before his death, of the beautiful bride won by the lance and the nails — John the Evangelist —
Sits beside him. And beside the other rests the leader under whom the ungrateful, fickle, and stubborn people lived on manna — Moses.
Opposite Peter, you see Anna seated, so content to gaze upon her daughter that she does not move her eyes even while she sings Hosanna.
And opposite the oldest father of the household sits Lucia — she who moved your Lady to action when you were bending your brow toward ruin.
But since the moments of your vision are flying, let us stop here, as a good tailor does — cutting the gown according to his cloth.
And let us turn our eyes to the First Love, so that, looking toward Him, you may penetrate as far as possible into His radiance.
But truly, lest perhaps you fall backward, thinking to advance by beating your own wings, you must obtain grace through prayer.
Grace from the one who has the power to help you. And you shall follow me with your heart's love, so that your spirit does not stray from my words."
And he began his holy prayer.

chapters.title: Paradiso, Canto XXXIII
paragraphs: "Virgin Mother, daughter of your Son, humble and exalted beyond any other creature, the fixed goal of the eternal counsel,
You are the one who ennobled human nature so greatly that its Creator did not disdain to make Himself its creature.
Within your womb the love was rekindled whose warmth, in the eternal peace, caused this flower to blossom.
Here, to us, you are the noonday torch of charity. And down among mortals, you are the living fountain of hope.
Lady, you are so great and so prevailing that whoever wants grace and does not run to you would have his desire fly without wings.
Your loving-kindness not only answers the one who asks, but many times it freely anticipates the asking.
In you is compassion, in you is pity, in you is magnificence. In you is gathered whatever goodness exists in any creature.
Now this man, who from the lowest pit of the universe all the way up to here has seen the spiritual lives one by one,
Implores you, through grace, for the power to lift his eyes still higher toward the ultimate salvation.
And I, who never burned for my own seeing more than I burn for his, offer you all my prayers and pray they be enough,
That you may scatter from him every cloud of his mortality with your prayers, so that the Supreme Joy may be revealed to him.
And further I pray you, Queen who can do whatever you will, that after so great a vision you preserve his affections sound.
Let your protection overcome his human impulses. See Beatrice, and all the blessed — they clasp their hands to you, seconding my prayer!"
The eyes beloved and revered by God, fixed upon the one who prayed, showed us how dear to her are devout prayers.
Then they turned to the Eternal Light — into which it is not credible that any creature's eye could ever penetrate so clearly.
And I, who was now approaching the end of all desires, ended within myself, as I should have, the burning of my longing.
Bernard was gesturing to me, smiling, that I should look upward. But I was already doing of my own accord what he wished.
For my sight, becoming purified, was entering more and more into the ray of the High Light which in itself is true.
From that point on, what I saw exceeded all speech, which yields to such a vision, and memory yields to such excess.
As one who sees something in a dream, and after the dream the feeling it imprinted remains while the rest fades from the mind,
Just so am I. For my vision has almost entirely ceased, yet the sweetness born from it still distills within my heart.
So the snow melts in the sun. So the prophecies of the Sibyl, written on light leaves, were lost upon the wind.
O Supreme Light, who rise so far above mortal thought, lend back to my mind a little of what you appeared to be,
And give my tongue such power that it may leave behind even one single spark of your glory for the people yet to come.
For by returning somewhat to my memory, and by sounding even faintly in these verses, more of your triumph will be grasped.
I believe the keenness of the living ray I endured would have struck me blind, had my eyes turned away from it.
And I remember that for this reason I was emboldened to bear more of it, until I joined my gaze with the Infinite Goodness.
O abundant grace, through which I dared to fix my sight upon the Eternal Light until my seeing was consumed within it!
I saw that in its depth, far down, is bound with love into a single volume everything that is scattered in leaves throughout the universe.
Substance and accidents and their relations — all fused together in such a way that what I speak of is a single, simple light.
I believe I saw the universal form of this knot, because in saying this I feel my joy expand.
A single moment brings me more oblivion than twenty-five centuries have brought to the enterprise that made Neptune marvel at the shadow of the Argo.
So my mind, held wholly in suspense, gazed steadfast, motionless, intent — and with gazing grew ever more enkindled.
In the presence of that light, a person becomes such that it is impossible to consent to turn away from it for any other sight.
Because the good that is the object of the will is gathered entirely within it, and outside it, whatever is perfect there is defective.
From here on, my words will fall even shorter of what I still remember than an infant's who still wets his tongue at the breast.
Not because more than a single, undivided semblance was in the living light I gazed upon — for it is always what it was before —
But through my sight, which was growing stronger as I looked, that single appearance was changing as I myself was changed.
Within the deep and luminous substance of the High Light, three circles appeared to me, of three colors and one dimension.
The second seemed reflected by the first, as rainbow is by rainbow. And the third seemed fire breathed equally from both.
O how feeble is speech, and how inadequate to my vision! And my vision, compared to what I saw, is so far from sufficient that to call it 'little' says too much.
O Eternal Light, who dwell solely in yourself, who alone know yourself, and, known to yourself and knowing yourself, love and smile upon yourself!
That circle which, so conceived, appeared in you as a reflected light — when my eyes had contemplated it for some time —
Seemed to me, within itself and in its very own color, to be painted with our human likeness. And so my sight was entirely absorbed in it.
Like the geometer who sets himself to square the circle and cannot find, no matter how he thinks, the principle he needs,
Such was I before that new sight. I wished to see how the image conformed to the circle and how it found its place there.
But my own wings were not enough for that — except that my mind was struck by a flash of lightning in which its wish came true.
Here power failed the lofty imagination. But already my desire and my will were being turned, like a wheel that is moved evenly,
By the Love that moves the sun and the other stars.
